breakfast.name: Chereh
instructions: Steam couscous until fluffy and let it cool slightly.
Pour sour milk or yogurt over the couscous.
Add sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Mix well until evenly combined.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.
breakfast.description: Steamed couscous mixed with sour milk and sugar, a traditional Gambian breakfast staple.

breakfast.name: Akara
instructions: Drain the soaked black-eyed peas and rub off the skins.
Blend the peas with onion, pepper, and salt into a thick paste.
Whip the paste with a spoon until light and airy.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the oil and fry until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
breakfast.description: Crispy black-eyed pea fritters, a protein-rich Gambian breakfast eaten with bread or porridge.

breakfast.name: Akara (Black-Eyed Pea Fritters)
instructions: Soak black-eyed peas, rub off skins
Blend into a smooth, thick paste with onion and pepper
Season with salt
Beat the batter vigorously — incorporating air makes them fluffy
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil — they puff into golden balls
Fry until golden on all sides — 3-4 min
Drain on paper
Serve hot with porridge or bread — the Gambian breakfast standard
The puff and the crunch are the hooks
breakfast.description: The Gambia's morning fritters — black-eyed pea batter fried into golden puffs. Found across West Africa but the Gambian version is distinctly seasoned. The puffing technique and the bean-to-fritter transformation are viral street food content.

breakfast.name: Chereh (Couscous Porridge)
instructions: Steam millet couscous until fluffy
Mix with cold sour milk or yogurt
Sweeten with sugar
Add baobab powder for tang and nutrition if available
Serve cold or at room temperature
This is a Gambian staple breakfast — tangy, filling, fast
The millet-and-sour-milk combination is ancient West African nutrition
breakfast.description: Gambian millet couscous mixed with sour milk — an ancient, tangy, probiotic breakfast. Baobab powder adds superfood status. The fermented-milk-and-grain concept has gained viral attention in the health food community as Africa's original probiotic breakfast.

lunch.name: Benachin
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season fish or chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot and fry the protein until browned, then set aside.
In the same oil, fry onions until golden, then add tomato paste and blended tomatoes.
Cook for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil separates.
Add water, bay leaves, and pepper, bring to a boil.
Add vegetables and cook for 10 minutes.
Add rice and the browned protein, stir gently.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until rice absorbs all the liquid.
Serve on a large platter.
lunch.description: Gambia's famous jollof rice, a festive one-pot dish of rice cooked in a rich tomato sauce with vegetables and protein.

lunch.name: Domoda
instructions: Heat oil and brown the meat on all sides.
Add onions and cook until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and chopped tomatoes, cook for 5 minutes.
Add peanut butter and water, stir until smooth.
Add sweet potato, pumpkin, and pepper.
Simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until meat is tender and sauce thickens.
Season with salt and serve over steamed rice.
lunch.description: A rich peanut butter stew with meat and root vegetables, one of Gambia's most cherished traditional dishes.

lunch.name: Domoda (Peanut Butter Stew)
instructions: Brown meat, set aside
Sauté onion, garlic, add tomato paste — fry until dark
Add peanut butter, stir until dissolved
Add water for desired consistency
Return meat, add pumpkin or sweet potato
Simmer 30-40 min until meat is tender and sauce is thick
Season with Scotch bonnet, Maggi, salt
Serve over white rice — the peanut sauce should pool around the rice
Domoda is The Gambia's national dish — the most-eaten meal in the country
lunch.description: The Gambia's national dish — peanut butter stew with meat and vegetables over rice. Every Gambian family eats domoda regularly, and the rich, nutty sauce is the country's comfort food. The 'peanut butter in a stew?' reaction from outsiders always goes viral as they discover it's genius.

lunch.name: Benachin (Gambian Jollof Rice)
instructions: Make tomato base: fry onion in palm oil, add tomato paste and fresh tomatoes, cook until thick
Add fish or meat, cook in the sauce
Add vegetables — root vegetables first, cabbage last
Add rice and water — the rice cooks in the sauce, absorbing all flavors
Cover tightly, cook on low — do not stir or lift the lid
The bottom layer scorches slightly — this is the prize, called 'tahray'
The rice should be red-orange from the tomato and palm oil
Serve from the pot — everyone gathers around and eats from the same dish
lunch.description: The Gambia's version of jollof rice — called 'benachin' (meaning 'one pot'). The word 'jollof' actually comes from the Jolof people of the Senegambia region, making The Gambia the origin story of the most debated dish in Africa. The 'original jollof' claim is The Gambia's viral food card.

lunch.name: Superkanja (Okra Soup)
instructions: Heat palm oil, sauté onion
Add smoked fish, fresh protein
Add sliced okra — the slimy texture is the point, not a flaw
Add dawadawa for funky depth
Add Scotch bonnet, garlic
Simmer until okra is soft and the soup is thick and slimy
Season with Maggi, salt
Serve with rice or fufu — scoop and swallow
The sliminess is the feature, not the bug — it helps the fufu slide down
lunch.description: The Gambia's okra soup — and yes, it's supposed to be slimy. The okra's mucilage is what makes it work with fufu (helping it slide down without chewing). Superkanja with dawadawa has a deeply savory, funky depth that converts skeptics. The 'it's supposed to be slimy' explanation goes viral every time.

dinner.name: Yassa Poulet
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Grill or broil the chicken pieces until lightly charred.
Heat oil in a large pot and cook the sliced onions slowly until very soft and golden.
Add the marinated chicken and any remaining marinade to the onions.
Add vinegar and the Scotch bonnet pepper.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Garnish with green olives and serve with rice.
dinner.description: Lemon and onion marinated chicken, a tangy and savory dish celebrated across the Gambia and Senegambia region.

dinner.name: Supakanja
instructions: Heat palm oil in a pot and sauté onions until translucent.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add okra and stir continuously for 10 minutes.
Pour in water and add dried shrimp and smoked fish.
Add the Scotch bonnet pepper and simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir in spinach and cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve over steamed rice or fufu.
dinner.description: A thick okra and seafood stew cooked with palm oil, a hearty Gambian dinner rich in flavor.

dinner.name: Afra (Roadside Grilled Meat)
ingredients: Beef, lamb, or goat (cubed or in large pieces)
instructions: Grill meat over charcoal until charred on edges, juicy inside
Dice the grilled meat into small pieces on a wooden board — at the roadside stand
Mix with diced raw onion, mustard, salt, pepper, chili
Serve on paper or in bread
Afra stands appear at night — following the charcoal smoke leads you there
The roadside board-chopping and mixing is the show — done right in front of you
Every Gambian neighborhood has an afra spot — it's the night food
dinner.description: The Gambia's night food — charcoal-grilled meat chopped on a wooden board and mixed with raw onion and mustard right in front of you. The roadside performance and the smoky-mustardy combination have made afra viral as West Africa's most interactive street food experience.

dinner.name: Yassa Poulet (Lemon-Onion Chicken)
ingredients: 6 large onions (very thinly sliced — this is the star ingredient)
instructions: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, sliced onion, garlic, mustard, Scotch bonnet — overnight is best
Remove chicken, reserve marinade with all those onions
Grill or brown chicken pieces until golden
In a pot, cook the massive amount of marinated onions in oil until soft and golden
Add the mustard from the marinade, olives if using
Return chicken to the onion sauce, simmer 30 min until tender
The onion sauce should be thick and tangy — the lemon-onion combination is the soul
Serve over rice with the onion sauce ladled generously
The amount of onions is not a mistake — it IS the dish
dinner.description: Senegambian lemon-onion chicken — the staggering amount of onions (they ARE the sauce) slow-cooked with lemon juice and mustard creates something magical. Originally from Senegal but deeply beloved in The Gambia. The 'that's too many onions' reaction followed by 'oh my God this is incredible' is a viral food moment.

dinner.name: Ebbeh (Dried Fish Stew with Greens)
ingredients: Pumpkin or sweet potato leaves (or spinach)
instructions: Soak dried fish, clean and break into pieces
Sauté onion in palm oil, add tomatoes, garlic
Add dried fish and dawadawa
Add greens — pumpkin leaves, sweet potato leaves, or spinach
Simmer until greens are soft and sauce is thick
Season with Scotch bonnet, salt
Serve with rice or fufu
The dried fish provides intense umami, the dawadawa adds funky depth
This is everyday Gambian home cooking — not fancy, just deeply flavored
dinner.description: The Gambia's home-cooking staple — dried fish and leafy greens simmered in palm oil with dawadawa. Not glamorous, just deeply flavored everyday food that represents what most Gambians actually eat. The umami-bomb from dried fish and fermented locust beans is what makes Gambian food quietly exceptional.

snacks.name: Tapalapa Bread with Butter
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water, let sit for 10 minutes until frothy.
Mix the flours and salt in a large bowl.
Add the yeast mixture and knead into a smooth dough.
Let rise for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Shape into an oblong loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding.
Slice and serve warm with butter.
snacks.description: Crusty Gambian bread made with a blend of wheat and millet flour, perfect for snacking.

snacks.name: Tapalapa Bread
ingredients: Flour (mix of wheat, millet, and/or corn flour — the Gambian blend)
instructions: Mix flours — the multi-grain blend is what makes tapalapa different from French bread
Add yeast, water, salt, sugar — knead into soft dough
Let rise 45 min
Shape into baguette-like loaves
Bake in a wood-fired oven at high heat until crusty outside, soft inside
The crust shatters, the inside is airy but denser than a French baguette due to the millet/corn
Sold fresh at every corner bakery — the smell of baking tapalapa fills Gambian streets
Used for sandwiches (filled with beans, egg, or afra meat) or eaten with stew
snacks.description: The Gambia's multi-grain baguette — a mix of wheat, millet, and corn flour baked in wood-fired ovens. Crustier and denser than a French baguette, with a distinctive grain flavor. Tapalapa bakeries are on every corner, and the morning smell of fresh bread is the Gambian street soundtrack.

snacks.name: Chakery (Sweet Couscous Dessert-Snack)
instructions: Steam couscous until fluffy
Let cool completely
Mix with condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla, nutmeg
Add pineapple and raisins if desired
Chill thoroughly — serve cold
The sweet, creamy, grain-based dessert is refreshing and satisfying
Sold in bags at markets — Gambian street dessert
The cold, creamy texture on a hot day is pure relief
snacks.description: The Gambia's sweet couscous dessert — fluffy grains mixed with condensed milk, vanilla, and nutmeg, served ice-cold. Sold in plastic bags at every market. The concept of 'cold sweet couscous' and the refreshing effect in West African heat have made chakery viral in African dessert content.

snacks.name: Tapalapa Bread Sandwich
ingredients: Tapalapa bread (Gambian French bread — long, crusty, soft interior)
Filling: bean stew, or egg, or sardines with onion and pepper
instructions: Tapalapa is The Gambia's daily bread — baked in wood-fired ovens across the country
Split the long crusty loaf
Fill with bean stew (the most traditional filling), or fried egg, or sardines with spicy onion
Add raw onion and Scotch bonnet for heat
The crusty bread against the soft, spicy filling is breakfast, lunch, and snack
Tapalapa bakeries are in every neighborhood — the smell of baking bread at dawn
This is The Gambia's most-eaten food — more than any single dish
snacks.description: The Gambia's tapalapa bread sandwich — the country's most-eaten food by far. Crusty wood-fired bread stuffed with bean stew, egg, or spicy sardines. Every neighborhood has a tapalapa bakery, and the dawn baking smell is The Gambia's alarm clock.

snacks.name: Chura Gerteh (Peanut-Couscous Energy Balls)
instructions: Roast peanuts, grind coarsely
Steam couscous until fluffy
Mix ground peanuts, couscous, sugar, butter
Shape into balls — press firmly so they hold together
These are Gambian energy balls — pre-workout fuel before the term existed
Eaten as snacks, breakfast, or sustenance for travel
The peanut-couscous combo is protein + carb in perfect balance
No cooking required — this is portable Gambian food
snacks.description: Gambian peanut-couscous energy balls — roasted ground peanuts mixed with steamed couscous and shaped into portable balls. Pre-workout fuel before the concept existed. The ancient Gambian energy food has gone viral as the original 'protein ball.'

desserts.name: Chakery
ingredients: Diced pineapple and raisins for topping
instructions: Steam couscous until fluffy, then spread on a tray to cool.
In a large bowl, whisk together condensed milk, yogurt, cream, sugar, vanilla, and nutmeg.
Fold the cooled couscous into the cream mixture.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until well chilled.
Top with diced pineapple and raisins before serving.
Serve cold in individual cups or bowls.
desserts.description: A creamy chilled couscous pudding mixed with sweetened milk, a popular Gambian party dessert.

desserts.name: Wonjo (Hibiscus-Mint Ice Pops)
instructions: Brew strong hibiscus tea with mint
Sweeten with sugar
Let cool, pour into molds or bags
Freeze until solid
The deep red color makes stunning popsicles
Sold as 'ice wonjo' at schools and markets — the cheapest frozen treat in The Gambia
The hibiscus tang and the mint freshness make these addictive
desserts.description: Frozen hibiscus-mint popsicles — ruby-red, tangy, and refreshing. The Gambia's cheapest frozen treat, sold at every school gate and market. The stunning red color and the natural-ingredient simplicity have made ice wonjo viral in the homemade-popsicle trend.

desserts.name: Chakery (Yogurt Couscous Pudding)
instructions: Cook couscous, let cool completely
Mix yogurt, condensed milk, evaporated milk, sugar, vanilla, nutmeg
Add cooled couscous to the cream mixture — stir gently
Add pineapple or raisins
Chill — serve cold
The texture is unique — tiny couscous grains in sweet, creamy, tangy yogurt
Chakery is The Gambia's celebration dessert — weddings, naming ceremonies, Ramadan
The cold, creamy, tangy combination is addictive
This has become viral as 'African yogurt pudding' — and it deserves the attention
desserts.description: The Gambia's celebration dessert — couscous folded into sweetened yogurt with condensed milk and fruit. Served at every wedding, naming ceremony, and Iftar during Ramadan. Chakery has gone viral as 'African yogurt pudding' and earned every bit of attention.

drinks.name: Wonjo (Hibiscus Tea)
instructions: Bring water to a boil and add hibiscus flowers and ginger.
Boil for 10 minutes, then remove from heat.
Strain into a pitcher and discard the flowers.
Stir in sugar and lime juice until dissolved.
Let cool, then refrigerate until chilled.
Serve over ice with fresh mint.
drinks.description: A vibrant ruby-red hibiscus drink flavored with ginger and lime, beloved across the Gambia.

drinks.name: Palm Wine
instructions: Collect fresh sap from the tapped palm tree in a clean calabash.
Strain through a clean cloth to remove any debris or insects.
Let sit for 4 to 8 hours to undergo natural fermentation.
Serve chilled or over ice.
Best consumed fresh the same day for a sweet, mildly fizzy taste.
drinks.description: Naturally fermented palm sap with a sweet and tangy flavor, a traditional alcoholic drink in the Gambia.

drinks.name: Wonjo (Hibiscus Drink)
instructions: Boil hibiscus in water until the liquid is deep ruby red
Strain, add sugar generously — it's a sweet drink
Add mint for freshness
Add pineapple juice or vanilla for variation
Chill — must be served ice cold
Wonjo is The Gambia's name for the West African hibiscus drink (bissap/zobo)
The color is photogenic — deep jewel red
Essential during Ramadan — every Iftar table has a jug of wonjo
The tartness quenches thirst like nothing else in the Sahel heat
drinks.description: The Gambia's wonjo — hibiscus flowers steeped into a deep ruby drink, sweetened and served freezing cold. Essential at every Ramadan Iftar and every celebration. The jewel-red color and the thirst-quenching tartness in Sahel heat make wonjo viral.

drinks.name: Baobab Juice (Bouye)
ingredients: Baobab fruit pulp (the chalky white powder from inside the fruit)
instructions: Soak baobab fruit pulp in water — it dissolves into a milky white liquid
Strain to remove seeds and fiber
Add sugar, vanilla or coconut milk
Chill — serve cold
Baobab has 6 times the vitamin C of oranges and more calcium than milk
The flavor is tangy, citrusy, slightly chalky — unique and refreshing
The baobab tree is Africa's 'tree of life' — the fruit is just one of its gifts
Bouye is The Gambia's health drink — long before 'superfood' was a word
drinks.description: Baobab juice — the chalky white pulp of Africa's 'tree of life' dissolved into a milky, tangy, citrus drink. Contains 6x the vitamin C of oranges. The Gambia's health drink for centuries before 'superfood' became a word. The origin story and nutrition facts are perpetually viral.
